rows.text: does nothing when `edx` is `0x1d` or more (signed); otherwise, with `S` = the dword at `rcx + edx*4 + 0x2c` (sign-extended index), calls `0020E600(S)` and stops when it returns null, else calls `0046F370(0020E600(S))` and `003697F0(0020E600(S))` (re-calling `0020E600` each time) and stores `0020E620(0)` back into that dword

calls `003590D0` with the incoming registers unchanged and passes its dword result to `003588B0`; when that returns null it returns 0, otherwise it tail-jumps (at `00343E20` + 0x1e) with `rcx` = that result and `edx` = 0

calls `002640C0` with the incoming registers unchanged (result `P`), calls `00267E10(r9)` twice (results `a` then `b`) and `00358940(P, b)`; when that returns non-null it stores the result of the call at `0034C630` + 0x4f with (`P`, that result, `a`) at dword `r8+8` and returns that call's result, else returns 0; on both paths it stores the `00358940` result (possibly null) at qword `[r8]`

calls `003589B0` with the incoming registers unchanged, then the call at `0035A1C0` + 0x14 with `ecx` = its dword result and `rdx` = the address of a stack dword it fills; returns 1 when that call returns non-zero and bit (`edx` mod 32, the incoming `edx`) of the filled dword is set, otherwise 0

walks the linked list starting at qword `+8` of the qword at `02EBEF88` (next at node `+8`, previous at node `+0`) and for every node whose byte `+0x13a` equals `cl` unlinks it (patching the neighbours, or the global's head `+8` / tail `+0x10`), calls `003A92D0(node)` and `003697F0(qword node+0x110)` when that qword is non-null, and scans at most 0x20 8-byte entries from `+0x18` of the same global, stopping at dword -1, for one whose dword equals node dword `+0x1c` and whose byte `+4` (zero-extended) equals signed byte node `+0x13b`; on a match it decrements word `+6` and, when that reaches 0 with bit `0x1` of byte `+5` set, shifts the following entries down one slot through the -1 terminator or index 0x1f, writes dword -1 at the last slot and calls `003A8130(dword node+0x1c, signed byte node+0x13b)`; each unlinked node is then passed to `003697F0`

calls `00421E20(rcx, word rdx+8, dword rdx+0xc, qword rdx+0x10)`; when it returns non-null it stores the result at qword `rdx+0x10` and dword 1 at `rdx+0x18`; returns the `00421E20` result on both paths

when dword `rcx+8` is -1 it only clears bit `0x2` of dword `[rcx]` and returns `rdx`; otherwise it calls `002ED570(rdx, dword rcx+8)` and, when that returns null, stores -1 at dword `rcx+8` and `0xffff` at word `rcx+0x14` (returning `0xffffffff`), then clears bit `0x2` of dword `[rcx]`; a non-null result is returned
calls `003589B0` with the incoming registers unchanged and tail-jumps (at `00473B30` + 0xf) with `ecx` = its dword result

notes: Callees not named on the page (0026AE90, 00265380, 00320CA0, 00290840) are cited by call site per rule (1). 003A87B0: the global at 02EBEF88 is read as a pointer (mov rdx,[rip+...]); the list head is qword +8 of that pointee and the tail qword +0x10 (stored when the unlinked node had no next). The entry match compares a zero-extended entry byte with a sign-extended node byte, so a node byte +0x13b of 0x80 or more never matches. The node is freed with 003697F0 whether or not an entry matched. 0035A1C0: the stack dword is the caller's home slot at rsp+0x40 (incoming rsp+0x10). 0046E950: the return values are what rax holds on each path (rdx copied into rax at entry, the 002ED570 result, or eax -1 zero-extended); callers may treat it as void. 0034C630: 002640C0 receives the incoming rcx/rdx/r8/r9 unchanged; whether it reads them is not shown.
